extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for determining patent term adjustment (PTA) and reductions under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and implementing regulations (37 CFR 1.703–1.705 and 1.704), including what constitutes applicant delay, IDS safe-harbors, what an application being "in condition for examination" means, and procedural requirements for reconsideration/reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of further prosecution via continuing application on PTA
rubrics_metrics.description: Further prosecution via a continuing application is a circumstance under 37 CFR 1.704 that can affect the period of adjustment; the period of adjustment set forth in § 1.703 shall not include any period that is prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution continues via a continuing application, any period prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent is excluded from applicant delay calculations for PTA. (Historical renumbering of this provision is discussed.)

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS-only paper safe harbor (37 CFR 1.704(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an information disclosure statement (IDS) in compliance with §§ 1.97 and 1.98, or an RCE (§ 1.114) with no submission other than an IDS, will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution if accompanied by a statement that each item in the IDS either (i) was first cited in any communication from a patent office in a counterpart foreign/international application or from the Office and that communication was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to filing of the IDS; or (ii) is a communication issued by a patent office in a counterpart foreign/international application or by the Office and that communication was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to filing of the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid PTA reduction for submitting IDS-only papers, the IDS must meet the cited provenance/receipt-time conditions. The thirty-day receipt window is strictly applied (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission form requirement for 37 CFR 1.704(d) statements (PTO/SB/133, PTA.IDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement required under 37 CFR 1.704(d)(1) must be submitted on Office form PTO/SB/133 using the appropriate document code (PTA.IDS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No changes to the statements on PTO/SB/133 may be made. Presentation of the form (by signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) constitutes a certification under § 11.18(b) that the existing text and any certification statements on the form have not been altered. For statements filed on or after July 17, 2023, inclusion of document code PTA.IDS is required; omission will result in treating the filing as if no 1.704(d) statement was filed unless a 1.705(b) reconsideration establishes otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thirty-day IDS receipt period non-extendable (37 CFR 1.704(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The thirty-day period set forth in paragraph (d)(1) (for IDS items originating from Office or foreign office communications) is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot extend the 30-day safe-harbor window; submissions outside this period will not qualify for the IDS-only safe harbor absent other relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reinstatement under 1.705(c) not deemed applicant failure (37 CFR 1.704(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission of a request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced patent term adjustment will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution under paragraph (c)(10) of § 1.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a reinstatement request itself does not create applicant delay for PTA purposes under the specified provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an application is "in condition for examination" (37 CFR 1.704(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when it includes: a specification with at least one claim and an abstract (§ 1.72(b)); papers in compliance with § 1.52; drawings (if any) in compliance with § 1.84; any required English translation (§ 1.52(d) or § 1.57(a)); a Sequence Listing in compliance with §§ 1.821–1.825 (if applicable) or Sequence Listing XML in compliance with §§ 1.831–1.835 (if applicable); an inventor’s oath or declaration or an application data sheet containing the information specified in § 1.63(b); the basic filing fee (§ 1.16(a) or (c)); the search fee (§ 1.16(k) or (m)); the examination fee (§ 1.16(o) or (q)); any certified copy required by § 1.57(a); and any application size fee required under § 1.16(s). For international applications entering the national stage, analogous items and fee citations (e.g., § 1.492 provisions) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed items must be present for the application to be considered in condition for examination. For international applications, national-stage-specific fee citations apply. This definition is the basis for the 8-month 'in condition' rule and other PTA reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to papers/drawings/sequence listings accepted up to latest reply before action or allowance (37 CFR 1.704(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is considered to have papers/drawings/Sequence Listing/Sequence Listing XML in compliance for purposes of 1.704(f) on the filing date of the latest reply (if any) correcting those items that is prior to the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may correct deficient papers up until the last reply before an examiner's action or notice of allowance; such timely corrections will be treated as present on the filing date of that latest reply for 'in condition' determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA reduction equals the applicant's period of failure and cannot exceed actual failure (Supernus-related amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made in view of Supernus Pharm. v. Iancu require that the period of reduction is equal to 'the period from the beginning to the end of the applicant’s failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution' and that the reduction cannot exceed the period of time during which an applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing reductions for applicant delay, do not reduce PTA beyond the actual days of applicant failure; reductions begin and end according to the specific start/stop rules for each type of failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start/end rules for applicant-delay reductions (cited paragraph specifics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific paragraphs of 37 CFR 1.704 define when reductions for applicant delay begin and end: e.g., 1.704(c)(2) was amended to end reduction on the earlier of the date a request to terminate a deferral was filed or the date the patent was issued; 1.704(c)(3) ends on the date a grantable petition to revive or accept late payment of the issue fee was filed; 1.704(c)(6) begins the reduction day after the date that is eight months from filing or national-stage commencement and ends when the preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper was filed; 1.704(c)(9) begins day after date of the PTAB or Federal court decision and ends on date amendment or other paper was filed; 1.704(c)(10) begins day after the mailing date of the notice of allowance and ends on the date the amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 or other paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these start/stop rules when computing applicant-delay reductions; each provision has its own triggering event and end point. See also the rule that if an amendment was expressly requested by the Office, applicant generally has three months to reply without incurring delay under 1.704(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file appeal brief within three months constitutes applicant failure (37 CFR 1.704(c)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 within three months from the date the notice of appeal was filed constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule applies to any application (other than design or reissue) where the notice of appeal is filed on or after the effective date; the three‑month period is strictly applied and previously inextensible under the regulation change.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.705(b) reconsideration request requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration of the patent term adjustment indicated on the patent must be an application for patent term adjustment filed no later than two months from the date the patent was granted (extendable under § 1.136(a)). The application for PTA reconsideration must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.18(e) and a statement specifying: the correct PTA and bases under § 1.702; the relevant dates per §§ 1.703(a)–(e) and adjustment per § 1.703(f); whether the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer and any expiration date; and either (A) any circumstances during prosecution constituting a failure per § 1.704 or (B) that there were no such circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration applications must include the indicated fee and a detailed factual statement establishing the claimed correct PTA and its statutory/regulatory bases. The two-month deadline is central but may be extended under § 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.705(c) requests for reinstatement of reduced PTA: requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for reinstatement of all or part of a period of adjustment reduced pursuant to § 1.704(b) for failing to reply within three months of the date of mailing of an Office communication must be filed prior to issuance of the patent (time not extendable). Such requests must be accompanied by the fee in § 1.18(f) and a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that, in spite of all due care, the applicant was unable to reply within three months. The Office will not grant more than three additional months for each reply beyond the three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires a 'due care' showing; the Director's satisfaction is required. The remedy is limited in duration (max three additional months per late reply).

rubrics_metrics.name: No third-party submissions/petitions on PTA considered (37 CFR 1.705(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: No submission or petition on behalf of a third party concerning patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) will be considered by the Office; such submissions will be returned or otherwise disposed of at the Office’s convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the patent owner/applicant may pursue PTA reconsideration or reinstatement per the regulation; third-party attempts to trigger PTA changes will not be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703(a)(1) — first action >14 months
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1.702(a) period of adjustment includes days, if any, beginning the day after the date that is fourteen months after the date the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (or national-stage fulfillment under 371) and ending on the mailing date of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)(i): count days after the 14‑month point until first Office action or notice of allowance (mailing date). For international/National Stage, the date the requirements of 371 are met controls the start date (discussion of PCT Articles 22/39 and 371(f) applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703(a)(2) — action >4 months after applicant reply (§ 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1.702(a) period of adjustment includes days, if any, beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date a reply under § 1.111 was filed and ending on the mailing date of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office issues an action more than four months after an applicant's reply under § 1.111, the excess time counts toward PTA under this subparagraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703(a)(3) — action >4 months after reply per § 1.113(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar to (a)(2), the period is days beginning the day after the date that is four months after the date a reply in compliance with § 1.113(c) was filed and ending on the mailing date of an action or notice of allowance, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies specifically to replies filed under § 1.113(c) (e.g., after an Office action), where Office delay beyond four months contributes to PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703(a)(4) — action >4 months after appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1.702(a) adjustment includes days beginning the day after the date that is four months after an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 was filed and ending on the mailing date of an examiner’s answer under § 41.39, an action under 35 U.S.C. 132, or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examination/Board response is delayed more than four months after applicant files an appeal brief, that excess period may be counted for PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703(a)(5) — action >4 months after final decision (PTAB/Federal court) where allowable claim remains
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustment includes days beginning the day after the date that is four months after the date of a final decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board or by a Federal court in an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141 or a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146 where at least one allowable claim remains, and ending on the mailing date of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable where litigation/Board decision leaves at least one allowable claim and the Office's subsequent action is delayed over four months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.703(a)(6) — action >4 months after issue fee paid/all outstanding requirements satisfied
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustment includes days beginning the day after the date that is four months after the date the issue fee was paid and all outstanding requirements were satisfied and ending on the date a patent was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent issuance is delayed more than four months after applicant has paid the issue fee and satisfied all outstanding requirements, those excess days count for PTA under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(b) — three-year applicant delay (general and exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1.702(b) period of adjustment is the number of days, if any, in the period beginning the day after the date that is three years after filing/national-stage commencement and ending on the date a patent was issued, but excluding certain periods (see subparagraphs (1)–(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three‑year metric is subject to multiple exclusions (RCE periods, interference/derivation periods, sealed condition periods, PTAB jurisdiction periods). See the specific subparagraphs for precise exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(b)(1) — exclusion for periods of RCE (37 U.S.C. 132(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude days, if any, in the period beginning on the date any request for continued examination (RCE) under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) was filed and ending on the date of mailing of the notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE pendency between filing and allowance is not counted toward the three‑year excessive delay measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(b)(2) — exclusion for interference or derivation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude days, if any, in the period beginning on the date an interference or derivation proceeding was instituted under 35 U.S.C. 135(a) and ending on the date that the interference or derivation proceeding was terminated with respect to the application; and exclude days for prosecution suspended by the Office due to interference/derivation proceedings not involving the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference/derivation institution and suspensions caused by such proceedings are excluded from the three‑year calculation. Separate counts for institution involving the application and suspensions not involving the application are defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(b)(3) — exclusions for sealed condition and secrecy orders (subitems i–iv)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude days the application was maintained in a sealed condition under 35 U.S.C. 181; days beginning on mailing of an examiner's answer under § 41.39 under a secrecy order until removal of the secrecy order; days beginning when applicant was notified that an interference/derivation would be instituted but for the secrecy order until removal of order; and days beginning on notification under § 5.3(c) and ending on the mailing of notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy order/ sealed-condition periods and related examiner-answer/suspension notification intervals are excluded from the three‑year PTA period.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(b)(4) — exclusion for PTAB jurisdiction transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude days, if any, in the period beginning on the date jurisdiction over the application passes to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under § 41.35(a) and ending on the date that jurisdiction by the PTAB ends under § 41.35(b) or the date of the last decision by a Federal court in an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141/civil action under 145, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When jurisdiction shifts to the PTAB, that period is excluded from the three‑year delay calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(c) — adjustment for interference/proceedings (two subperiods)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1.702(c) period of adjustment is the sum of (1) days from the date an interference/proceeding was instituted to involve the application under 35 U.S.C. 135(a) until termination with respect to the application; and (2) days from the date prosecution in the application was suspended by the Office due to interference/derivation proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 135(a) not involving the application until termination of the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These periods correspond to pendency of interference/derivation proceedings and suspensions that relate to PTA for proceedings-related delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(d) — adjustment for sealed condition/secrecy (four subperiods)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1.702(d) period of adjustment is the sum, to the extent not overlapping, of: (1) days the application was maintained in sealed condition under 35 U.S.C. 181; (2) days from mailing of an examiner’s answer under § 41.39 in the application under secrecy order until secrecy removal; (3) days from notification that an interference or derivation would be instituted but for the secrecy order until order removal; and (4) days from notification under § 5.3(c) until mailing of notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subperiods capture PTA due to secrecy/defense-related delays; overlaps must be avoided when summing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(e) — adjustment for PTAB jurisdiction to favorable final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1.702(e) period of adjustment is the sum of days from the date jurisdiction over the application passes to the PTAB under § 41.35(a) and ending on the date of a final decision in favor of the applicant by the PTAB or a Federal court in an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141 or a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PTAB jurisdiction culminates in a final favorable decision, the intervening days may be included in PTA under this subparagraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(f) — calculation rules, overlap, and effective date of adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjustment will run from the expiration date of the patent as set forth in 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2). To the extent that periods of delay attributable to grounds specified in § 1.702 overlap, the period of adjustment shall not exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed. The term of a patent entitled to adjustment under § 1.702 and this section shall be adjusted for the sum of the periods calculated under paragraphs (a) through (e), to the extent such periods are not overlapping, less the sum of the periods calculated under § 1.704. The date indicated on any certificate of mailing or transmission under § 1.8 shall not be taken into account in this calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute PTA as (sum of eligible delay periods under 1.703(a)–(e), avoiding overlaps) minus (sum of applicant delay periods under 1.704). Do not double-count overlapping delays; certificate-of-mailing dates do not control the calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Day-counting conventions for PTA periods (inclusion/exclusion rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a period is indicated as 'beginning' on a particular day, that day is included in the period (it is 'day one'). For purposes of 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A) and (B) (corresponding to 37 CFR 1.703(a) and (b)) the end of the period is 'day zero' for adjustment; whereas for proceedings/orders/reviews under 1.703(c)–(e) (corresponding to 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(C)(i)–(iii)), the first day of the proceeding/order/review is 'day one' of the period of adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these start/end day-counting conventions carefully when calculating PTA to avoid off-by-one errors; example provided in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a notification under 35 U.S.C. 132 (Office actions vs pre-exam notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain items are 'actions issued as a result of the examination conducted pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 131' and therefore are notifications under 35 U.S.C. 132 — specifically: a written restriction requirement, written election of species requirement, a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, an action under Ex parte Quayle, and a notice of allowability (PTOL-37). The Office treats such restriction requirements (even if containing no action on the merits) as notifications under 35 U.S.C. 132. Case law (Pfizer v. Lee; Idorsia Pharm.; Hengehold; Digital Equipment) supports treating written restriction requirements as notices under 132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PTA and statutory-deadline calculations, treat the listed restriction/election/Quayle/allowability items as 'Office actions' under 132. MPEP § 710.02(b) directs examiners to set a shortened two‑month statutory period for a written restriction requirement containing no action on the merits under 35 U.S.C. 133.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-examination processing notices are not notifications under 35 U.S.C. 132
rubrics_metrics.description: Office notices and letters issued as part of pre-examination processing are not notices issued as a result of the examination under 35 U.S.C. 131 and thus are not notifications under 35 U.S.C. 132. Examples: Notice of Incomplete Nonprovisional Application; Notice of Omitted Item(s) in a Nonprovisional Application; Notice to File Missing Parts of Application; Information Notice to Applicant; Notice to File Corrected Application Papers Filing Date Granted; Notice to Comply with Requirements for Patent Applications Containing Nucleotide/Amino Acid Sequence Disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat these pre-examination communications as triggering the timing rules associated with 35 U.S.C. 132 (e.g., the 14‑month first action measurement); they are administrative/process notices only.

rubrics_metrics.name: When international applications fulfill 35 U.S.C. 371 requirements for PTA start-date purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications, the fourteen-month measurement for 1.703(a)(1) begins on the later of: the date the application was filed under 111(a) or the date the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371 are fulfilled (which may be the date of commencement of the national stage under 371(b)/(f) or the date the requirements of 371(c) are met). If applicant files the required oath/declaration, filing fee, and any required English translation before expiration of PCT Article 22/39 time period but does not request early processing under 371(f), the requirements are met once the relevant PCT time period has expired. A clear express request under 371(f) is required to commence national stage earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international National Stage PTA calculations, determine the date 371 requirements are met carefully (PCT Article timing and 371(f) early processing rules apply). Use form PTO‑1390 or an express statement to request early processing under 371(f); a general remarks statement is insufficient.
